faq.q: What gets you a yellow card?
faq.a: A yellow card is a caution for things like a reckless tackle, diving, arguing with the referee, wasting time or fouling again and again.
asks: Why do players get yellow cards?

faq.q: What happens when you get a red card?
faq.a: You are sent off, must leave the pitch, and cannot be replaced, so your team plays with one fewer player. You usually miss the next match too.
asks: What does a red card mean?

faq.q: Do two yellow cards make a red card?
faq.a: Yes. A second yellow card in the same match means a red card, and the player is sent off.

faq.q: Who invented yellow and red cards?
faq.a: English referee Ken Aston had the idea while stopped at traffic lights. The cards were first used at the 1970 World Cup in Mexico.
asks: When were red cards first used?

faq.q: Why use cards instead of just talking?
faq.a: Players and fans speak many languages. A coloured card is understood by everyone in the stadium at once.
asks: Why does the referee show a card?

facts: Yellow and red cards were first used at the 1970 FIFA World Cup in Mexico.
Referee Ken Aston thought of the card system while waiting at a set of traffic lights.
